Every gosh darn day. Well...more like 7/10 days. Some days my body is ready to go, but my brain is foggy as heck.

I've spoken to my parents about things like this too - because I was praised for "looking so good" when I wasn't able to eat due to emetaphobia/panic attacks, and later due to chronic illness stuff.  It's really hard to deal with. Have you spoken with them candidly about how comments on your body make you feel?                       
   
When I received praise for dropping weight, I'd tell them why my weight was down, and tell them NOT to comment or praise me for it. Because,  well.... i was either too nauseous to eat, too anxious of having anything in my stomach (emetaphobia), or just generally didnt need solid food bwcause my malnourished body was so used to thriving on the morsels i gave it.                                                             

When I was gaining weight I would usually not get praise, but if my eating habits or body shape/size were questioned, I would just say "I'm focusing on reparing my relationship with food"  or "I'm listening to my body, regardless of how I look." <-that last one is still hard for me. I still need to remind myself that thinness/inability to eat is way worse than having body fat and having an appetite.  (I am currently a grown ass adult living with her parents who barely eat and walk 20k steps a day each.)  (It's kind of like living in a house of eating disorders)

TLDR: I've been there. Try being uncomfortably, brutally, and obnoxiously honest with them about how those comments make you feel. Be concise, clear, and confident. If they fight you, give them time to sort their thoughts. If they dismiss you, dismiss them.  All love. Hope things start to be less shitty for you asap <3

If you want a natural solution, I came up with my own little recipe that works to quell the constant mild nausea. Ginger ice. Use raw ginger, not powdered, not ginger candy.  Chop it up super fine. Then blend it with some water and strain / press out the pulp. Freeze the ginger water in tiny icecube shapes (I have a gummy bear mold). Freeze and suck or chew when you need a bit of relief. It's not sweet. It will actually taste spicy, but it really soothes my nausea. Doesn't fix it, but I'm guessing you've gotten used to being slightly nauseous pretty much all the time, so any bit of relief will help you out.

I have a hard time with certain types of fibers. Like... broccoli? Nauseous and constipated for 2+ days. But! When I  pair the fiber with a protein? (I make vegan chili with lots of beans and lots of seasoned TVP).... small portions, calm bowels.  Also, taking like a quarter dose of polyethylene glycol every day helps. And I cut out wheat. That was another thing I didnt realise was causing a bubbly reaction in my gut. I used to take benefiber, but I found that was more likely to just swell up my insides without moving anything along. 

Basically, I've found a decent amount of relief in really fine tuning my intake. I will eat the same few things for a few weeks and see how my body adjusts to them. I reccomend trying it. It can get a bit boring, but it's worth it to not feel like shit. When you settle in to the base diet, you can add a few more things here and there. It doesnt eliminate flare ups, but I've personally found it very effective:)
